   **9+. The economy, first phase** (decided 21 October 2026). Built after item 9 and before item 10, because people of the land (10+) measures room partly by the grain in a province's stores, item 11a's merchants and fees lean on markets, and the wealth of a realm, which the score counts from here on, means little until gold buys labour. From "Economy and resources": provinces produce grain, and gold where its mines were ("Mines are where they were", from the history pass), instead of yielding gold, with population fixed until 10+ makes it move; taxes in goods, at the default rate until 10+a gives the king the rate together with the hunger that answers it, go into each province's stores ("Production is local"); each city has a local market with engine-set prices, where kings sell their surplus for gold from the people's purse, which the pay of soldiers and workers flows back into, at prices set by one formula ("Markets", "Where gold comes from and where it goes", "Prices"); all gold a province brings in, mined or earned at its market, reaches the treasury at once, and from item 13 after its travel time ("One treasury, many stores"); how much an army carries and how fast stores spoil are marked first guesses; gold buys labour, so armies are paid in gold and fed with grain from what they carry, depots, caravans under scheduled orders, their hosts and the land, with hunger and then mutiny when none of it suffices (until loose men and bands exist, in items 10+ and 11, a mutinous unit simply disbands and its men go home) ("Gold buys labour", "Armies need food as well as pay", "Caravans carry a kingdom's goods"). Markets price large lots along the curve and settle each season's trades together; soldiers' pay buys everything but food and is spent only where an army stands by leave, so an invader forages and loots instead of paying the defender; and caravans, by land or as ships at sea with the fleets the game already has ("Ships carry goods"), may sell and buy at foreign markets they have passage to, paying tolls at borders, with exemptions by tablet and smuggling judged by item 7b's check for sneaking through a host's land ("Prices", "Where gold comes from and where it goes", "Caravans carry a kingdom's goods", "Tolls and smuggling"). A hungry army takes from the land wherever it stands, its own land included, and after a few seasons of hunger or missing pay it mutinies ("Armies need food as well as pay"). With stores and armies that eat comes the siege's clock: a blockaded city holds by its stores, its mouths and its water, and walls set the price of a storm ("How long a siege lasts"). In the pace rule, this item turns on size, load, pack animals and the slowest part ("What sets a company's pace"). Each province starts with a basic storage capacity from its towns, enough for its own needs and a modest depot; building raises it in a later phase ("Storage"). From this item strength is the wealth of the realm: the land by what it produces at reference prices, the gold in the treasury and the people's purses, and the goods in its stores and markets ("The wealth of a realm" under Victory); a bought city's price is what it adds, purse, stores and market included, and leaves the world, and item 11+ designs the rest of the scoreboard. The script kings learn to play it well in the same item, selling surplus, supplying armies and stocking depots ("Building it"), and the king's view summarizes stores, shortages and prices. First guesses, tuned in item 18.

   **Built in two parts** (decided 21 October 2026), each its own pull request with its own stop for review, since 9+ has grown into two items' worth:
   - **9+a. The economy at home.** Grain and gold produced by province, stores with their basic capacity, local markets with their prices and the people's purse, filled only by what is paid in, such as pay spent there and builders' pay ("What fills a people's purse"), with soldiers carrying savings home and kings able to feed their towns from their stores; taxes in goods at the default rate, since the king's own rate comes in 10+a with the hunger that answers it ("How a king lives"); one treasury, armies' food and pay with hunger and mutiny, caravans at home under scheduled orders, and the pace factors for size, load, pack animals and the slowest part. Strength becomes the wealth of the realm ("The wealth of a realm" under Victory), which changes built scoring, so the script kings' benchmarks are recorded before and after. Also sleep for human seats, as an automatic end of turn when nothing concerns them, woken by the same triggers as model seats and able to wake themselves at any time ("Per-seat sleep, never a global skip" under Pacing). **Stop for review.**
   - **9+b. The economy abroad.** Caravans and ships trading at foreign markets they have passage to; ships carrying cargo, with a starting harbour level on every coast; armies spending only where they stand by leave, and foraging and looting where they do not; tolls with a rate for each partner; and smuggling through item 7b's sneaking check. Built after 9+a. **Stop for review.**
